claims.statement: A focal skin swelling with uncertain contents can be assessed with targeted soft-tissue ultrasound.
claims.limitation: Society procedural guidance only; not a rule for deep-space or vascular lesions.

claims.statement: A discrete superficial cavity with mobile internal echoes and no internal flow supports a cutaneous collection when anatomy and examination agree.

claims.statement: A symptomatic accessible cutaneous pus collection generally needs incision and drainage for source control rather than aspiration or an antibiotic change as a replacement.
claims.limitation: Adjunctive antibiotic selection is a separate decision; no universal no-antibiotic conclusion.

claims.statement: Diffuse skin infection without a collection is managed through a nonpurulent antimicrobial pathway rather than an incision into inflamed tissue.

claims.statement: Persistent infection associated with retained foreign material needs that local source addressed as part of source control.

claims.statement: An aseptically collected tissue specimen is preferred to a superficial swab when culturing a suspected diabetic foot soft-tissue infection.

claims.statement: Initial evaluation of possible diabetic foot osteomyelitis integrates probe-to-bone examination, plain radiographs and inflammatory biomarkers.
